title: Private install smoke harness for quotas, IAM, DNS, and GPU capacity
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description: Build an automated smoke harness that runs as a pre-install and upgrade gate for Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. The harness will exercise Terraform/IaC outputs and cloud APIs to validate account quotas, required IAM roles and policies, DNS delegation and resolution for internal control plane endpoints, and GPU capacity/availability for requested SKUs. The harness should be runnable by the onboarding automation and also as a standalone CLI for SREs and solutions engineers. Results must produce a machine-readable report (JSON), a human-readable summary, and structured remediation guidance with links back to the exact Terraform modules or configuration lines that need changes.
acceptance_criteria: A single CLI command (or GH Action) runs the full harness against a target AWS/GCP account and returns exit code 0 for pass and non-zero for failures
IAM checks enumerate missing or insufficient policies and point to the minimal policy diff needed
Quota checks verify availability for EC2 instance types (including specific GPU SKUs), ENI limits, EBS quota, and account-wide API quotas and surface shortfalls
DNS checks confirm hosted zone delegation, internal control-plane DNS A/ALIAS records, and pod-to-control-plane resolution within a sample VPC namespace
GPU capacity probe validates available SKUs in the target region and verifies requested CUDA/cuDNN driver compatibility where applicable
Harness emits a JSON report with structured failure codes, remediation hints, and links to related Terraform modules/PRs
checklist: Design CLI interface and JSON schema for output
Implement Terraform module scanner to map module outputs to required resources
Implement IAM policy linter and live permission probe (STS assume + simulated actions)
Add quota checks for EC2/GCE, ENIs, EBS, and service limits
Add DNS validator that performs both zone delegation and in-VPC resolution tests
Implement GPU SKU availability and driver-compatibility checks using cloud capacity APIs
Wire harness into onboarding GH Action and add optional Slack webhook/console alert
Create automated tests and sample accounts for regression testing
steps_to_run: 2) Configure credentials: export AWS_PROFILE=redwood-test; export TF_OUTPUT_PATH=./tfstate.json
4) Review JSON report + human summary at ./reports/latest-summary.txt
5) If failures, follow remediation links in the report to Terraform module lines or Confluence runbook

risks_and_tradeoffs: Risk: Using live cloud APIs can be rate-limited — added caching and backoff, but initial runs against large organizations may still hit limits
Tradeoff: We will start with read-only probes that may not detect implicit grants from org-level SCPs; full coverage requires coordination with customer Security/Infra teams
Risk: Exposing account IDs and ARNs in logs — implement strict redaction and allow customers to opt out of sending full reports to Redwood SaaS
Tradeoff: Running driver compatibility checks requires instance spin-ups in some cases; to avoid cost/latency we will use SKU metadata first and optionally run a cheap probe instance in a sandbox
